name: Pacific Ocean
summary: The largest and deepest ocean, covering about a third of Earth's surface.
overview: Larger than all land combined. Ringed by the 'Ring of Fire' of subduction zones, volcanoes and the deepest trenches.
geography: Bounded by Asia and Australia to the west and the Americas to the east. Holds the Mariana, Tonga, Kuril–Kamchatka, Philippine and Kermadec trenches.
water: The El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) in the tropical Pacific drives global climate variability. It holds the largest oxygen minimum zones (eastern tropical Pacific).
life: The Coral Triangle (the world's peak marine biodiversity), the Clarion-Clipperton Zone nodule fields, and hadal snailfish.
human: The largest tuna fisheries. Island nations depend heavily on it.
threats: Deep-sea mining in the CCZ, warming, bleaching, plastics (the Great Pacific Garbage Patch).

name: Atlantic Ocean
summary: The second-largest ocean, split down the middle by the Mid-Atlantic Ridge and home to the AMOC.
overview: An S-shaped basin widening by a few cm a year along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge.
geography: Between the Americas and Europe/Africa. Includes the Caribbean, Gulf of Mexico, Mediterranean and North Sea as marginal seas.
water: The Gulf Stream and AMOC carry heat north. The North Atlantic is a key site of deep-water formation.
life: Lost City hydrothermal field, the Sargasso Sea (eel spawning), cold-water coral reefs.
human: Historic cod, herring and tuna fisheries. Major shipping lanes.
threats: AMOC weakening, overfishing, hurricanes intensified by warm water.

name: Indian Ocean
summary: The warmest ocean, ruled by monsoon reversals of winds and currents.
overview: Enclosed to the north by Asia, so it lacks a northern polar connection.
geography: Between Africa, Asia, Australia and the Southern Ocean. Includes the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal.
water: Monsoon-driven seasonal current reversal (Somali Current). The Indian Ocean Dipole affects rainfall in India, Africa and Australia.
life: Coelacanths, whale sharks of the Maldives, scaly-foot snails at vents.
human: Crucial for Indian, East African and Indonesian fisheries and trade.
threats: Fastest-warming ocean, bleaching, oxygen loss in the Arabian Sea.

name: Southern Ocean
summary: The ring of ocean around Antarctica, driven by the strongest current on Earth.
overview: Recognised as the fifth ocean by the IHO in 2000 and by National Geographic in 2021.
geography: South of ~60°S around Antarctica.
water: The Antarctic Circumpolar Current moves ~100+ million m³/s. It forms Antarctic Bottom Water and takes up a large share of anthropogenic heat and CO₂.
life: Krill, penguins, colossal squid, Antarctic toothfish, icefish (with no haemoglobin).
human: Managed by CCAMLR. Krill and toothfish fisheries.
threats: Sea-ice loss, warming, acidification, krill fishing.

name: Arctic Ocean
summary: The smallest, shallowest ocean, losing its summer sea ice fast.
overview: Surrounded by Eurasia and North America, with wide continental shelves.
geography: Connected to the Atlantic via the Fram Strait and to the Pacific via the Bering Strait.
water: A fresh, cold surface layer over warmer Atlantic water. Summer sea-ice extent has fallen sharply since 1979.
life: Narwhals, belugas, polar bears, Greenland sharks.
human: New shipping routes and resource interest as ice retreats.
threats: Ice loss, 'Atlantification', pollution transported from lower latitudes.

name: Mediterranean Sea
summary: A nearly enclosed sea with unusually warm, salty deep water and a long human history.
overview: Connected to the Atlantic by the 14 km-wide Strait of Gibraltar. It nearly dried out during the Messinian salinity crisis (~5.9–5.3 million years ago).
geography: Between Europe, North Africa and Western Asia.
water: Evaporation exceeds inflow, so it is very salty. Deep water stays ~13 °C, much warmer than most of the deep ocean.
life: Posidonia seagrass meadows, monk seals, bluefin tuna spawning grounds. A biodiversity hotspot with many endemics.
human: Over 150 million coastal inhabitants and heavy tourism.
threats: Marine heatwaves, invasive species via the Suez Canal, overfishing, plastics.

name: Caribbean Sea
summary: A tropical sea of coral reefs and the deepest point of the Caribbean, the Cayman Trough.
overview: Bounded by the Antilles island arcs and Central/South America.
geography: Contains the Mesoamerican Reef, the second-largest barrier reef system.
water: Warm surface waters fuel Atlantic hurricanes.
life: Reef fish, sea turtles, invasive lionfish, the world's deepest known vents (Beebe vent field, ~5,000 m).
human: Tourism and fisheries economies.

name: Gulf of Mexico
summary: A basin of natural oil seeps, brine pools and a large seasonal 'dead zone'.
overview: Partly enclosed by the US, Mexico and Cuba.
geography: Fed by the Loop Current and the Mississippi River.
water: Nutrient runoff from the Mississippi creates a large hypoxic zone each summer.
life: Brine pools with 'hot tub of despair' lakes, cold seeps, giant isopods.
human: Major oil and gas region. Deepwater Horizon spill in 2010.

name: Sargasso Sea
summary: The only sea without coastlines, defined by currents and floating Sargassum seaweed.
overview: Bounded by the currents of the North Atlantic Gyre.
geography: Mid-North Atlantic around Bermuda.
water: Calm, clear and warm. Sargassum mats float at the surface.
life: The spawning ground of European and American eels, and a nursery for turtles.
human: Hamilton Declaration (2014) for conservation cooperation.
threats: Plastic accumulation in the gyre, shipping.

name: North Sea
summary: A shallow, heavily used shelf sea between Britain and mainland Europe.
overview: Formed over a drowned landscape (Doggerland) flooded after the last ice age.
geography: Between the UK, Norway, Denmark, Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium and France.
water: Shallow and well-mixed, with strong tides.
life: Herring, cod, harbour porpoises, grey seals.
human: Oil and gas, the largest offshore wind build-out in the world, shipping.
threats: Bottom trawling (high carbon disturbance), heavy shipping.

name: Baltic Sea
summary: A young brackish sea with some of the largest dead zones on Earth.
overview: Formed after the last glaciation and still rising due to post-glacial rebound.
geography: Enclosed by Scandinavia, the Baltic states, Poland, Germany, Russia and Finland.
water: A low-salinity surface over a salty, often anoxic deep layer.
life: Few species tolerate brackish water. Grey seals, cod (in decline).
human: Shipping and fishing.

name: Black Sea
summary: The largest anoxic body of water on Earth: below ~150–200 m there is no oxygen.
overview: A meromictic sea: the layers never mix fully.
geography: Between Eastern Europe, the Caucasus and Anatolia, linked to the Mediterranean through the Bosporus.
water: Hydrogen-sulfide-rich deep water preserves ancient shipwrecks remarkably well.
life: Life mostly confined to the upper ~150 m. Dolphins, anchovy.
human: Fisheries and strategic shipping.

name: Red Sea
summary: A young ocean in the making, with heat-tolerant corals and hot brine pools.
overview: Africa and Arabia are rifting apart here.
geography: Between Africa and the Arabian Peninsula; connected to the Indian Ocean (Bab-el-Mandeb) and the Mediterranean via the Suez Canal.
water: Very salty and warm. Deep water stays ~21 °C.
life: Corals unusually tolerant of heat, brine-pool microbes.
human: One of the busiest shipping routes (Suez).

name: Arabian Sea
summary: Home to one of the world's thickest oxygen minimum zones, driven by monsoon upwelling.
overview: Bounded by India, Pakistan, Iran and the Arabian Peninsula.
geography: North-western Indian Ocean.
water: Summer monsoon upwelling drives huge productivity and a deep oxygen minimum zone.
life: Lanternfish swarms, whale sharks, the Arabian humpback whale (a resident, isolated population).
human: Fisheries and shipping to the Gulf.
threats: Expanding low-oxygen zones, cyclones intensified by warming.

name: Bay of Bengal
summary: The world's largest bay, freshened by the Ganges–Brahmaputra and fuelling strong cyclones.
overview: Receives enormous river discharge and sediment (the Bengal Fan, the largest submarine fan).
geography: Bounded by India, Bangladesh, Myanmar and Sri Lanka.
water: A freshwater lid causes strong stratification, which favours cyclone intensification.
life: Mangrove Sundarbans, Irrawaddy dolphins, olive ridley turtle mass nesting (arribadas in Odisha).
human: Dense coastal populations and fisheries.
threats: Cyclones, sea-level rise, oxygen minimum zone.

name: Coral Sea
summary: Home to the Great Barrier Reef, the largest coral reef system on Earth.
overview: Off north-east Australia.
geography: Between Australia, Papua New Guinea, the Solomon Islands and Vanuatu.
water: Warm tropical waters.
life: The Great Barrier Reef (~2,300 km). The Ocean Census found many new species here in 2025–26.
human: Tourism and a protected marine park.

name: South China Sea
summary: A biodiverse and contested sea crossed by a large share of global shipping.
overview: Bounded by China, Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia.
geography: Western Pacific marginal sea.
water: Monsoon-driven circulation.
life: Extensive reefs (Spratlys, Paracels) and large fisheries.
human: A major trade route.
threats: Reef destruction by island building, overfishing, territorial disputes.

name: Sea of Japan (East Sea)
summary: A semi-enclosed sea that forms its own deep water, like a mini-ocean.
overview: Enclosed by Japan, Korea and Russia.
geography: Western Pacific.
water: Forms its own deep water in winter, which is weakening with warming.
life: Squid fisheries, Japanese spider crabs nearby.
human: Fisheries.

name: Bering Sea
summary: One of the most productive seas on Earth, supporting huge pollock and crab fisheries.
overview: Between Alaska and Russia, connecting to the Arctic via the Bering Strait.
geography: North Pacific.
water: Seasonal sea ice drives a rich spring bloom.
life: Walrus, fur seals, king crab, pollock.
human: A major share of US seafood landings.
threats: Sea-ice loss leading to crab population crashes (2021–22).

name: Weddell Sea
summary: A major source of Antarctic Bottom Water and the resting place of Shackleton's Endurance.
overview: Off the Antarctic Peninsula and Coats Land.
geography: Southern Ocean.
water: Brine rejection from sea ice forms some of the densest water on Earth.
life: Icefish nesting colonies (~60 million nests found in 2021), emperor penguins.
human: A proposed marine protected area.

name: Ross Sea
summary: Often called the most pristine marine ecosystem left, and protected by a large MPA since 2017.
overview: A deep bay of the Southern Ocean beside the Ross Ice Shelf.
geography: Antarctica.
water: Polynyas drive high productivity.
life: Antarctic toothfish, Adélie and emperor penguins, Weddell seals.
human: Ross Sea region MPA (~1.55 million km²).

name: Persian Gulf
summary: A hot, hyper-saline shallow sea whose corals survive extremes that kill corals elsewhere.
overview: Between the Arabian Peninsula and Iran.
geography: Indian Ocean (via the Strait of Hormuz).
water: Summer surface temperatures above 35 °C.
life: Heat-tolerant corals, dugongs.
human: Oil and gas, desalination.

name: Tasman Sea
summary: Between Australia and New Zealand, a marine-heatwave hotspot.
overview: South-western Pacific.
geography: Bounded by Australia and New Zealand.
water: The East Australian Current pushes warm water south.
life: Range shifts of tropical species southward.
human: Fisheries.

name: Hudson Bay
summary: A huge inland sea where polar bears depend on seasonal ice.
overview: In north-eastern Canada.
geography: Linked to the Arctic and Atlantic.
water: Ice-covered for most of the year.
life: Polar bears, belugas.
human: Indigenous communities.

name: Barents Sea
summary: The Arctic's 'hot spot' of warming, where Atlantic water is pushing north.
overview: North of Norway and Russia.
geography: Arctic shelf sea.
water: 'Atlantification' as warm Atlantic water reduces sea ice.
life: The world's largest cod stock, king crab (introduced).
human: Major fisheries, oil and gas.

name: Caspian Sea
summary: The largest enclosed inland body of water, salty but not connected to the ocean.
overview: A remnant of the ancient Paratethys Sea.
geography: Between Europe and Asia.
water: Brackish. Its level is falling.
life: Beluga sturgeon (source of caviar), Caspian seals.
human: Oil and gas.
